usageNotes: Creates a new SDN zone object in the cluster-wide SDN configuration. The required `zone` identifier must be 2–8 alphanumeric characters starting with a letter, and `type` must match the intended networking model (e.g., `evpn` for BGP/EVPN overlay, `vlan` for simple VLAN-backed networks). After creating the zone you must call `put_cluster_sdn` (apply pending SDN changes) before the zone becomes active on any node; zone-type-specific params (controller, peers, vrf-vxlan, exitnodes, etc.) are only relevant for the matching type.

examples.summary: Create a simple VXLAN zone across two cluster nodes

tips: Zone IDs are cluster-global and immutable after creation — choose a short, descriptive name up front.
For EVPN zones, a BGP controller must already exist (post_cluster_sdn_controllers) before referencing it via `controller`.
VXLAN zones require `peers` (node IPs) and should set `mtu` to 50 bytes below the underlay MTU to account for VXLAN encapsulation overhead.
After any SDN object create/update, run `put_cluster_sdn` to push pending changes; nodes will not see the zone until the config is applied.
The `dhcp: dnsmasq` option requires the dnsmasq package to be installed on each participating node.
